neutral: Judge whether the supplied records support the proposed complete identity interpretation. Use only supplied causal measurements and their source, age, reliability and conflicts. Distinguish observations, estimates, prior judgments and identity claims. Lack of contradiction is not positive identity evidence. Missing fields remain unknown. Respect complete occupancy and unchanged records. Returning DEFER does not certify H0. The questions are independent; answer each from state.
fish_rules: The observations are predicted fish masks in a circular tank. Similar depths can be indistinguishable rather than evidence of the same fish. A merged mask can jointly contaminate depth and appearance; these are not independent votes. Native and public identities are claims. A new native handle can be a previously observed fish returning. Recent clean core depth is not automatically invalid merely because an interaction occurred; retain its recorded original eligibility and age. Occupied identities cannot be taken without explaining where their prior occupant belongs and why its old claim is contradicted. A swap needs positive evidence for both new edges and traceable contradiction of both replaced nontransient claims. One-to-one assignments and repeated agreement do not prove identity. Missing surfaces and fully occluded fish are not current observations. No fixed object count licenses inventing or deleting a mask.
examples: Synthetic policy A: Two records have indistinguishable reliable depth and no distinguishing appearance. Uniqueness alone cannot choose their identities; DEFER is appropriate.

Synthetic policy B: A new handle agrees with a free old reference across applicable reliable evidence after occlusion. The old source is traceable and competing explanations are contradicted. A complete reconnection can be supported without treating the new handle as a new physical fish.
Synthetic policy C: A proposal takes an occupied identity but gives no contradiction for its established occupant. A stronger new edge alone does not authorize the proposal.
Synthetic policy D: A putative swap explains one new edge well but the other lacks evidence. Reject authorization of the complete swap; never execute half.

Synthetic policy E: A recent clean core sample retains its original native-survivor eligibility during an interaction, while whole-mask measurements are mixed. Preserve the qualified core evidence with its provenance; do not certify the mixed whole mask or invent a hidden surface.
